title: Recipe Source Card
user: A home cook saving web recipes who needs a clean, editable, source-attributed card without retyping ingredients or trusting a black-box scrape.

evidence.quote_or_summary: The recipe-app launch receives 74 comments, including reports that a common search such as 'Anti-inflammatory' crashes the app, showing how brittle broad recipe products can become.
The user story asks to paste a recipe URL, parse schema.org Recipe JSON-LD, map ingredients where possible, and open a pre-filled edit screen so recipes do not need retyping.

recurrence: A large recipe-app discussion and a separate 2026 feature request both point to capture reliability and editability as the real repeated task.
current_workaround: Browser bookmarks, screenshots, copy/paste into Notes, or importing into an opaque recipe app and correcting it by hand.
incumbents_and_gap: Paprika, Mela, Tandoor, and Mealie import recipes, but import failures and hidden transforms make provenance and repair difficult. The gap is a small capture tool that keeps the source, parsed fields, and user edits visible together.
smallest_useful_product: A local browser extension that extracts Recipe JSON-LD, preserves the canonical URL and attribution, shows a field-by-field editable preview, and exports JSON/Markdown. Non-goals: copying full sites without permission, a hosted recipe catalog, paywall bypassing, or AI rewriting.
success_measure: At least 85% of pilot imports create a usable card after fewer than three field edits, and every exported card retains its source URL.
monetization: one-time — source-preserving personal capture is a durable local utility with no server operating cost.
constraints: Respect site terms and robots boundaries; import only structured metadata exposed to the user; retain attribution and URL; do not redistribute copyrighted recipe text as a shared corpus.
why_distinct: It is a transparent, repairable personal capture pipeline, not a recipe database or thin LLM summarizer.
